kernel.name: list_manuals
kernel.description: List top-level Manuals (manual_id, name, description, source) from the controller: first the read-only Cybion Common Manual (source "common"; product usage guidance compiled into the controller), then the user's own Manuals (source "local"). Content is intentionally omitted; use load_manual to bring a Manual and its direct children into the Thread.

kernel.name: cybion_list_workers
kernel.description: List owned and shared Workers (worker_id, label, owner_user_id, access) from the controller. Every Worker tool call must include an exact worker_id from this list; never choose a Worker implicitly. Registered Workers are not necessarily online; availability is checked when a Worker tool is called.

kernel.name: load_manual
kernel.description: Bind a Manual to this Thread so the Controller keeps it loaded. The full Manual JSON arrives in a developer message right after this call, and the Controller delivers a newer copy by itself whenever the Manual changes or a compaction replaces the history, so the Thread never opens it again to stay current. The copy already carries the Manual, its Use When description, its body, and its direct children. Use it for material the Thread must keep working from across manual windows; list_manuals stays the way to find what exists. Resolves local Manuals first, then the read-only Cybion Common Manual. A Thread holds 12 loaded Manuals by default; its own setting or the account default may allow more or fewer, and a load past the cap is refused with the count and the cap — unload_manual releases one.

manual_id.description: Exact manual_id from list_manuals, from children inside a loaded Manual's JSON, or from a Manual this Thread already knows.

kernel.name: unload_manual
kernel.description: Release a Manual this Thread loaded, which stops the Controller from refreshing it. The copy already in the conversation stays until the next compaction and is no longer maintained, and a notice tells the Thread not to rely on it; load_manual brings it back. Answers unloaded: false when the Manual was not loaded in this Thread.

manual_id.description: Exact manual_id of a Manual this Thread loaded.

kernel.name: write_manual
kernel.description: Create or edit one of the user's local Manuals from the controller — title, Use When description, body, and parent. Omit manual_id — or send null or an empty string, which count as omitted — to create a new Manual: name is required and it starts at the top level or under parent_id. Pass manual_id to edit that Manual; omitted fields keep their current values, and parent_id takes an exact manual_id, null for the top level, or the special value "TRASH" to move the Manual into the trash (updates only). A trashed Manual disappears from every Manual tool, while the user still sees it in the Manuals page and can restore it. Returns the Manual metadata. The read-only Cybion Common Manual cannot be written, and a Manual hidden by the trash cannot be written until it is restored. A Manual its owner locked refuses every write_manual change — title, Use When description, body, parent, and TRASH — and answers with its child Manuals, which stay writable.

manual_id.description: Omit (or pass null or an empty string — all three count as omitted, so a caller that fills every property still creates) to create a new Manual; pass the exact id of an existing local Manual to edit it, from list_manuals or from the children of a Manual this Thread has loaded.

name.description: Title, 1-160 characters. Required when creating; omit to keep the current title when editing.

description.description: Use When description — the condition for when this Manual should be read (up to 10,000 characters). Omit to keep the current description, or for an empty one when creating.

content.description: Markdown body (up to 200,000 characters). Omit to keep the current body, or for an empty one when creating.

parent_id.description: Parent: an exact manual_id to become a child of that Manual, null for the top level, or "TRASH" to move the Manual into the trash where the user can still see and restore it (updates only). Omit (or pass an empty string) to keep the current parent, or to create at the top level.

kernel.name: cybion_list_ultimate_machines
kernel.description: List the user's Ultimate Machines (终极机器): scheduled self-checks that run one bash command on a Worker every interval and stay silent while the command exits 0. A failing run is delivered into the machine's repair Thread (终极机器 · <name>) as a user message asking to make the command return 0 — dropped, not queued, while that Thread is mid-turn; an offline or missing Worker is reported once per episode through Linkit; a run that never settles is declared lost after 15 minutes and reported once. Returns id, name, worker_id, worker_label, command, intent, interval_seconds, enabled, last_run_at, last_exit, thread_id, created_at. Use it to pick a machine_id for cybion_get_ultimate_machine, cybion_set_ultimate_machine or cybion_delete_ultimate_machine.

kernel.name: cybion_get_ultimate_machine
kernel.description: Read one Ultimate Machine by machine_id: its definition (name, worker_id, command, intent, interval_seconds, enabled), its bound repair Thread, and the latest settled run — last_run_at plus last_exit, where 0 is healthy, any other number is the Unix exit code (a command killed without one counts as -1), and null means the latest run produced no exit code (no run yet, a run lost mid-flight, or an execution error reported through Linkit). Use it to inspect a machine before editing it, or to relate a 【终极机器·<name>】 repair request to the machine that sent it.

kernel.name: cybion_set_ultimate_machine
kernel.description: Create or update an Ultimate Machine (终极机器) — one bash command run on one Worker every interval_seconds, silent while the command exits 0. Omit machine_id to create: name, worker_id, command and interval_seconds are required, the first run starts right away, and a repair Thread named 终极机器 · <name> is created automatically. Pass machine_id to update — only the fields you give change, and: an empty intent clears it; enabled pauses or resumes; a new worker_id starts a fresh offline-notification episode; renaming retitles the repair Thread unless the user renamed it by hand. Machines are removed with cybion_delete_ultimate_machine, not here; pausing with enabled=false also stops the repair Thread's in-flight turn. To validate a check immediately, run the same command with bash on the Worker — the next scheduled run re-verifies silently.

machine_id.description: Omit to create a new machine; pass the exact id from cybion_list_ultimate_machines to update that machine.

name.description: Label shown in the Ultimate Machines list, 1-120 characters, e.g. 磁盘检查. On create required.

worker_id.description: Exact worker_id from cybion_list_workers, of a Worker you own — shared Workers cannot run machines. The command runs there through the normal Worker protocol (bash with timeout_seconds=300). On create required; changing it moves the machine and restarts the offline-notification episode.

command.description: The single bash command run every interval; 1-4000 characters. Exit 0 means healthy and silent; any other result is sent to the repair Thread with the tail of stderr/stdout (up to 1500 characters), so make failures self-explanatory. Keep it cheap and safe to repeat. On create required. Example: test $(df -Pk / | awk 'NR==2 {print $5}' | tr -d %) -lt 90

intent.description: Optional plain-language goal of the check, up to 2000 characters, e.g. 确保根分区低于 90%. Delivered with every repair request (意图) so the fixing agent knows what the check protects. On update, omit to keep it and pass an empty string to clear it.

interval_seconds.description: Seconds between runs, 10-2592000 (30 days). The first run starts right after creation; afterwards the next run starts one interval after the previous run settled, with at most one run in flight. On create required.

enabled.description: Update only: false pauses all runs and notices and stops the repair Thread's in-flight turn, true resumes. A new machine starts enabled.

kernel.name: cybion_delete_ultimate_machine
kernel.description: Delete an Ultimate Machine (终极机器) for good: it leaves the machines list, stops being scheduled, and a run still in flight settles silently. The bound repair Thread (终极机器 · <name>) and its whole history survive as an ordinary Thread — delete that Thread separately if the user wants it gone too. The machine cannot be restored; use this only when the user asked to remove it, and prefer pausing with cybion_set_ultimate_machine when they merely want it quiet. Returns {"deleted": true, "machine": <the deleted definition>}.

machine_id.description: Exact id of the machine to delete, from cybion_list_ultimate_machines.

note.name: add_notes
note.description: Add sticky notes on the user's notes list: one line per note, one action per note. A note is a debt — it stays there until it is crossed out, so add one only when something is genuinely owed and do not add background, plans, or reminders to yourself. Every note attaches to this Thread: only this Thread sees it and only this Thread can cross it out, so it may lean on this conversation's manual. Notes past the limit are refused; cross out or tear off what is done first.

text.description: One action in one short line. The service refuses text past its character limit and asks you to condense it.

note.name: cross_out_notes
note.description: Cross out sticky notes you finished. Crossing out is the only way a note leaves the list: there is no delete, no edit and no reopen, and a note attached to another Thread is reported as not_found. Crossing an already crossed note is reported as already_done and changes nothing, so never retry it.

items.description: Exact note id from the injected sticky notes block.

worker.name: bash
worker.description: Run a shell command on the user's selected Worker. To wait before the command runs, set delay_seconds instead of embedding a `sleep`: embedded sleeps count toward Worker call duration and misreport Worker performance.

summary.description: One short sentence, in the user's language, saying why you are making this call. It is shown on the call card as the intent summary, so state the goal, not the command.

delay_seconds.description: Seconds to wait in the controller before this call starts. Prefer this over a `sleep` command: a shell sleep counts toward Worker call duration and misreports Worker performance.

timeout_seconds.description: Seconds to allow the command to run before the Worker kills it, measured from execution start; the delay_seconds wait does not count. Defaults to 600.

worker.name: browser_control
worker.description: Control an isolated browser on the user's selected Worker. delay_seconds waits in the controller before the action starts.

summary.description: One short sentence, in the user's language, saying why you are making this call. It is shown on the call card as the intent summary, so state the goal, not the command.

delay_seconds.description: Seconds to wait in the controller before this call starts.

worker.name: computer_use
worker.description: Perform a user-device computer action through the selected Worker. delay_seconds waits in the controller before the action starts.

summary.description: One short sentence, in the user's language, saying why you are making this call. It is shown on the call card as the intent summary, so state the goal, not the command.

delay_seconds.description: Seconds to wait in the controller before this call starts.

worker.name: view_image
worker.description: Read an image file (PNG, JPEG, WebP, or GIF) from the selected Worker's filesystem and attach it to this conversation so you can see it. Use it whenever you need to look at a picture, diagram, screenshot file, or photo that lives on the Worker; files larger than 4 MiB must be resized first (for example with bash).

summary.description: One short sentence, in the user's language, saying why you are making this call. It is shown on the call card as the intent summary, so state the goal, not the command.

path.description: Path of the image file on the Worker.

delay_seconds.description: Seconds to wait in the controller before this call starts.

normai_web_search.name: normai_web_search
normai_web_search.description: Search the web and return the result sources (title, URL, and snippet). Use it whenever the user asks about current events, recent releases, prices, or any fact that may have changed since your knowledge; run more searches when one query is not enough, and cite the sources in your reply.

query.description: The search query, written like a search engine query. Split complex questions into several targeted searches.

normai_image_generation.name: normai_image_generation
normai_image_generation.description: Generate an image from a text prompt and attach it to this conversation for the user to see. Use it whenever the user asks for a picture, illustration, diagram, or any other visual. Describe the subject, style, colors, and composition fully in the prompt. To edit or derive from pictures the user attached to their input, pass the one-based positions of those pictures in reference_images (for example [1] for the first attached picture, at most 4); without reference_images it creates a new image from the prompt alone.

prompt.description: Complete description of the image to generate.

reference_images.description: One-based positions of the pictures attached to the user's input to use as references, for example [1] for the first attached picture. Omit to create a new image from the prompt alone.

normai_audio_transcription.name: normai_audio_transcription
normai_audio_transcription.description: Transcribe an audio recording attached to this Thread. Pass the audio_ref of the attachment; add prompt (topic, setting, names) and keywords to fix terms and acronyms the provisional transcript got wrong, or pass another model. Call it again with better hints when the transcript looks wrong.

audio_ref.description: The audio_ref of an audio attachment in this Thread's input.

prompt.description: Free-form context to guide recognition: topic, domain vocabulary, participant names, spelling of terms. Context only, not instructions.

keywords.description: Terms and acronyms that must appear verbatim.

language.description: ISO-639-1 language hint such as zh or en; omit to auto-detect.

model.description: Speech-to-text model override; defaults to the Thread's configured model.
